recent_posts.title: Photonics advance could enable compact, high-performance lidar sensors
recent_posts.summary: MIT researchers have developed a novel silicon-photonics chip design that could enable compact, solid-state lidar sensors with no moving parts. The key innovation is an array of integrated antennas with varied geometries and different propagation coefficients, allowing them to be placed close together without coupling — reducing crosstalk from ~100% to ~1%. This enables wide field-of-view beam steering without grating lobes or noise penalties, overcoming a fundamental limitation of existing optical phased array (OPA) designs. The advance could benefit autonomous vehicles, aerial surveying, and construction monitoring.

recent_posts.title: Rett syndrome study highlights potential for personalized treatments
recent_posts.summary: MIT researchers at the Picower Institute used 3D human brain organoids to study two distinct MECP2 mutations causing Rett syndrome — R306C and V247X — and found they produce different structural, activity, and connectivity abnormalities. Using three-photon microscopy and single-cell RNA sequencing, the team identified mutation-specific molecular defects: HDAC2 overexpression in R306C and reduced GABA receptor expression in V247X. Crucially, each mutation responded to a different drug treatment — an HDAC2 inhibitor for R306C and the GABA agonist baclofen for V247X — demonstrating that even single-gene disorders may require personalized therapeutic approaches based on the specific mutation involved.

recent_posts.title: Powering 160,000 hours of discovery at MIT.nano
recent_posts.summary: MIT.nano has transitioned from the aging CORAL platform to NEMO, an open-source laboratory management system originally developed at NIST. The new system centralizes tool reservations, training workflows, safety compliance, and communications for over 1,500 researchers using 200+ instruments that collectively log 160,000 hours of work annually. NEMO's modular architecture and plugin framework allow deep customization and integration with MIT's existing digital infrastructure, including authentication and billing. MIT.nano collaborated with NEMO's project lead and MIT IT teams to handle cleanroom-specific challenges. As one of the largest NEMO deployments globally, MIT.nano's enhancements are now benefiting other research facilities worldwide.

recent_posts.title: MIT CSAIL builds 3D-printed Y-zipper that switches objects between soft and rigid states
recent_posts.summary: MIT CSAIL researchers have revived a 1985 patent concept by William Freeman to create a three-sided 'Y-zipper' fastener. Using a custom software design tool and 3D printing with PLA or TPU plastics, users can customize and fabricate these triangular zippers that seamlessly switch objects between soft and rigid states. Applications include faster tent assembly, adjustable medical wrist casts, motorized robotic limbs, and dynamic art installations. Stress tests showed the zippers survived 18,000 open/close cycles before breaking, with durability attributed to their elastic stress-distributing structure. Future directions include metal versions, larger-scale fabrication, and potential use in disaster relief shelters and space exploration.

recent_posts.title: How chromatin movement helps control gene expression
recent_posts.summary: MIT researchers used MINFLUX super-resolution microscopy to measure chromatin movement across seven orders of magnitude in timescale — from hundreds of microseconds to several hours — for the first time. They identified two distinct classes of chromatin dynamics: one where chromatin moves in a constrained, subdiffusive manner within roughly 200 nanometers, and another where chromatin moves more freely but only over longer timescales. The constrained movement means genes and regulatory elements within ~100,000 base pairs can find each other routinely without additional mechanisms. The findings challenge existing models (Rouse and fractal globule) and reveal unexpected cell-type-specific differences in chromatin behavior, with implications for understanding gene regulation and DNA repair.

recent_posts.title: Found Industries aims to strengthen America’s industrial supply chains
recent_posts.summary: Found Industries, founded by MIT alumnus Peter Godart, is expanding beyond its aluminum fuel technology to launch Found Metals, a division focused on extracting gallium and other critical metals domestically. With 99% of global gallium supply controlled by China and recent Chinese export restrictions, the company developed an electrochemical extraction process from Bayer liquor as a byproduct of solving its own supply chain vulnerability. Backed by a $5.4M DOE program, Found plans to produce gallium, indium, and germanium by end of 2027, while continuing to scale its aluminum-water catalytic reactor systems for industrial heat and power generation.

recent_posts.title: Testing sustainable agriculture in Barcelona
recent_posts.summary: Twelve MIT students participated in a three-week Independent Activities Period course in Barcelona exploring regenerative agriculture, cooperative economies, and the degrowth movement. Led by Professor Kate Brown, the course was offered as a MISTI Global Classroom and took students beyond traditional learning — visiting farms, cooking meals for migrants at a community squat, and rebuilding a greenhouse at an eco-resort. Students engaged with local cooperatives, pig farmers, and urban gardens rooted in over a century of Catalan cooperative tradition. The experience reshaped students' views on climate change, community-driven solutions, and alternatives to capitalist development models.

recent_posts.title: Beacon Biosignals is mapping the brain during sleep
recent_posts.summary: Beacon Biosignals, founded by MIT alumni, has developed an FDA-cleared EEG headband that collects clinical-grade brain activity data while patients sleep at home. The company partners with pharmaceutical companies to run clinical trials for conditions like Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, schizophrenia, and narcolepsy. Machine learning processes the sleep data to detect disease progression, monitor drug effects, and identify patient cohorts. Beacon is building a large-scale brain foundation model from this data, aiming to enable earlier detection of neurological diseases — potentially before symptoms appear. The company recently acquired an at-home sleep apnea testing firm serving 100,000+ patients and raised $97 million to expand its platform.

recent_posts.title: MIT postdoc applies algebraic combinatorics to theoretical physics
recent_posts.summary: Amanda Burcroff, an MIT School of Science Dean's Postdoctoral Fellow, researches algebraic combinatorics with the goal of applying combinatorial techniques to theoretical physics. Her work includes proving positivity properties of generalized cluster algebras — structures relevant to particle physics and string theory — and unifying different mathematical frameworks. At MIT she works with Professor Alexander Postnikov and aims to extend her methods to areas like mirror symmetry. She is also active in math outreach for underrepresented groups.

recent_posts.title: MIT researchers directly map 3D atomic structure of relaxor ferroelectrics for the first time
recent_posts.summary: MIT researchers have directly characterized the 3D atomic structure of relaxor ferroelectrics for the first time, using a technique called multi-slice electron ptychography (MEP). These materials are widely used in ultrasounds, microphones, and sonar systems, but their internal atomic structure had never been directly measured. The study revealed a hierarchy of chemical and polar structures spanning atomic to mesoscopic scales, and found that polarization regions are much smaller than existing models predicted. By feeding experimental data back into computer simulations, the team refined models that can better predict material behavior — with implications for next-generation memory storage, sensing, and energy technologies.

top_posts.title: Deep-learning model predicts how fruit flies form, cell by cell
top_posts.summary: MIT researchers developed a deep-learning model that predicts cell-by-cell development during fruit fly embryo formation with 90% accuracy. The model uses a dual-graph structure representing cells as both point clouds and foam-like bubbles, tracking properties like position, division, and folding minute-by-minute during gastrulation. The approach could eventually predict development in more complex organisms and identify early disease patterns in conditions like asthma and cancer, though high-quality video data remains the primary limitation for broader applications.

top_posts.title: How MIT's online program helped a nonprofit leader apply data driven policy in Indonesia
top_posts.summary: Munip Utama leveraged MIT's MicroMasters Program in Data, Economics, and Design of Policy to strengthen his work at Baitul Enza, a nonprofit supporting disadvantaged students in Indonesia. Coming from a lower-middle-class background, he gained rigorous training in data analysis, economic reasoning, and evidence-based policy design. He now applies these skills to design case-based learning modules, mentor youth researchers, and improve program effectiveness through data-driven approaches. Financial assistance and income-based pricing enabled him to complete the program while managing resource constraints at his volunteer-run organization.

top_posts.title: MIT concrete supercapacitor achieves 10x energy storage improvement
top_posts.summary: MIT researchers have developed an improved concrete-based supercapacitor (ec³) that stores 10 times more energy than previous versions by optimizing electrolytes and manufacturing processes. The material combines cement, water, carbon black nanoparticles, and electrolytes to create a conductive network within concrete structures. A cubic meter can now store over 2 kilowatt-hours of energy, reducing the volume needed for household daily energy needs from 45 to 5 cubic meters. The technology could enable buildings, roads, and infrastructure to function as energy storage systems, supporting renewable energy adoption and potentially charging electric vehicles or powering off-grid homes.

top_posts.title: A new strategy to cope with emotional stress
top_posts.summary: Research from MIT's McGovern Institute reveals a cognitive strategy focused on social good can help individuals cope with distressing events, potentially effective for emergency personnel frequently exposed to high-stress situations. The study compared this method with the well-known 'distancing' technique and found both were effective at reducing negative emotions, although distancing generally showed a stronger effect. However, the social good approach may be more practical in scenarios where distancing is not feasible, and older adults tend to apply these strategies more effectively due to greater life experience in emotion regulation.

top_posts.title: MIT student overcomes rural background to excel in signal processing and teaching
top_posts.summary: MIT graduate student Titus Roesler overcame a challenging start from a rural background without AP classes to become an award-winning teaching assistant and mentor. His teaching work helped him master signal processing, where he now focuses on compressed sensing applications in high-frequency radio communications. Through roles as a TA for multiple classes and designing seminars, he developed expertise in source separation problems, including a project separating harmonies in Bach chorales using Python.
